A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MS-GS research, with matching methods, benchmarks, and substantial appendix overlap. All 18 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v4 are readable, including their equations, tables, figures, and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original novel-view synthesis experiments on three datasets, component ablations, initialization comparisons, and appendix analyses of camera alignment and evaluation metrics.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds depth-alignment measurements, a 12-view evaluation, and quantitative appearance-initialization results.

M1.justification: Section 3, the losses, Algorithm 1, and near-zero appearance initialization are retained. However, v4 Appendix A.3 newly states that initialization combines MVS points with back-projected points, whereas v1 does not identify MVS inputs. The PDFs do not establish whether this is an added method component or a previously omitted implementation detail.

E1.justification: Both evaluate sparse Mip-NeRF 360, the same three Phototourism monuments, and three drone scenes with four appearances. The 12-view experiment changes sample count within existing coverage; the depth check and failure examples analyze retained scenes rather than introducing a new dataset or task domain.

E2.justification: v4 adds SPARS3R to the Mip-NeRF 360 comparison in Table 2. SPARS3R also replaces DNGS in the corresponding qualitative panel, from v1 Figure 4 to v4 Figure 5; DNGS remains in Table 2. The other established comparison sets are retained, including DUSt3R in Table 5.

E3.justification: v4 adds a 12-view drone evaluation using three images per appearance alongside the retained 20-view setting. It also introduces a bonsai depth-accuracy evaluation using dense-view MVS depth as a reference and mean absolute error as the metric. The main registration protocols, image-quality metrics, and training schedule remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 substantially expands diagnostic evidence with direct semantic-alignment accuracy validation, a stronger sparsity test, and failure examples for incomplete initialization and specular surfaces. Table 6 adds quantitative support to the existing appearance-initialization analysis. The original component-ablation visualization is moved into the main text, while initialization-transfer, camera-alignment, and metric-sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Reporting continues to use scene averages and camera-error means and medians; the added result rows do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises MS-GS GT-pose PSNR from 21.96 to 22.39 and in-the-wild LPIPS from 0.248 to 0.238, among other values. Table 3 revises NeRF-W GT-pose PSNR from 16.52 to 16.95. Substantial new entries cover SPARS3R, appearance initialization, 12-view performance, and depth accuracy. New findings include alignment MAE of 1.94 versus 1.07 and 12-view PSNR of 17.78 for MS-GS versus 14.83 for GS-W. The causes of the revised main-table values are unspecified.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, alignment formulas, and camera-frame construction are retained. Equation 9 is reformatted and its scalar/vector notation clarified without changing the construction. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs that are added or removed.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that semantic depth alignment and geometry-guided virtual-view supervision improve sparse-view, multi-appearance reconstruction, and both introduce the drone benchmark and in-the-wild evaluation protocol. The expanded conclusion restates these contributions rather than establishing a new central claim.

C2.justification: v4 expands the transient-object caveat into a dedicated limitations section explaining why uncertainty masks struggle with sparse observations. It adds non-Lambertian highlight smoothing and artifacts outside densely initialized regions, illustrated in Figure 10. It also gives a more specific explanation of WildGaussians absorbing photometric errors through appearance adjustment and uncertainty weighting.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies 12 drone test images and registration using hloc, SuperPoint, and RoMa. Appendix A.3 discloses combined MVS/back-projected initialization and narrows the reported result hardware from RTX A5500 and A100 to RTX A5500. Architecture, thresholds, loss weights, and the 16,500-iteration schedule are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds focused positioning against SPARS3R and MASt3R, contrasting their pointmap-based initialization with monocular depth. It also adds citations supporting 3D warping, registration tools, and possible lighting or surface-modeling extensions. The broader related-work organization and positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: v4 edits terminology, grammar, and cross-references, expands the conclusion, and separates limitations into their own section. The appendix is reorganized around a new dataset-description section, with implementation and algorithm sections reordered. Most introductory and methodological prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: Figure 1 corrects the mismatched bicycle ground truth in the church comparison and updates that example. The appendix ablation becomes main-text Figure 4, reformatted from a two-by-two grid into one row. Figure 5 expands the benchmark montage with a low-light example and SPARS3R. New dataset, depth-error, and failure-case figures, plus two new result tables, substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The SPARS3R comparison, direct depth-accuracy check, 12-view test, and concrete failure cases strengthen validation and clarify applicability. Correcting Figure 1 also improves the reliability of the visual evidence. These are useful gains, but unexplained main-table updates and ambiguity about the newly disclosed MVS initialization limit the improvement in reproducibility.
